title: Measles cases in 2026 are set to surpass last year's total. Here's why
snippet:
In the decade before the measles vaccine became available, the CDC estimates that 3 to 4 million in the U.S. were sickened by measles every year, about 48,000 were hospitalized and about 400 to 500 people died. About 1,000 people suffer encephalitis every year. [...] The number of reported measles cases in the United States this year is soon set to surpass the total reported for all of last year.

title: Amid Cyclosporiasis Outbreak, Measles Cases Are Nearing Last Year's Total - Forbes
snippet: # U.S. Measles Cases Reach Over 2,200—Nearly Totaling All Measles Cases Recorded In 2025. As an outbreak of the diarrhea-inducing illness cyclosporiasis grows this month, the spread of measles in the U.S. this year is outpacing the case count for the entirety of 2025, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which reported this week that cases of the highly contagious disease has reached 2,231. The 2,231 cases were confirmed as of July 9, according to CDC data, meaning the U.S. is just 58 cases away from logging the 2025 total. The CDC has found 93% of this year’s cases are linked to people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. ## What States Are Most Impacted By Measles This Year? Cyclosporiasis, a parasitic illness that causes diarrhea, has infected well over 1,500 people in the U.S., with an outbreak centered in Michigan. Last year’s outbreak resulted in three deaths, the first of which marked the first recorded death from measles in the U.S. in a decade.

title: US measles cases surpass 2,000 for the 2nd year in a row: CDC - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
snippet: # US measles cases surpass 2,000 for the 2nd year in a row: CDC. So far this year, 2,030 cases have been recorded in 38 states and D.C. ByMary Kekatos and Georgia Davis. Measles cases in the United States have surpassed 2,000 for the second year in a row, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). So far in 2026, 2,030 confirmed cases have been recorded in 38 states and the District of Columbia, CDC data shows. The U.S. also saw its first measles deaths in more than a decade last year, including two among unvaccinated school-aged children in Texas and one among an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico. The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. Meanwhile, 4% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.

title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years - BBC
snippet: The US has hit a 35-year high in measles cases, according to new figures from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The US has seen 2,318 confirmed cases of measles in 2026, just seven months into the year, up from last year's high of 2,289, when two unvaccinated children died of the disease. The rising number of cases have come as vaccine hesitancy in the US has increased in recent years, leading to lower immunisation rates. The US has recorded more measles cases over the past 18 months than the total number over 25 years before that. Over the past month, Virginia and Pennsylvania have been dealing with new measles outbreaks, while the state of Utah is still responding to a cluster of infections that began last year. Earlier this year, a federal judge blocked the US government from implementing a series of sweeping changes to childhood immunisations under Kennedy's leadership, including slashing the number of recommended shots for children from 17 to 11.

title: Measles
snippet:
Before the introduction of measles vaccine in 1963 and widespread vaccination, major epidemics occurred approximately every two to three years and caused an estimated 2.6 million deaths each year.

An estimated 95 000 people died from measles in 2024 – mostly children under the age of five years, despite the availability of a safe and cost-effective vaccine. [...] WHO continues to strengthen the Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network (GMRLN) to ensure timely diagnosis of measles and track the virus’ spread to assist countries in coordinating targeted vaccination activities and reduce deaths from this vaccine-preventable disease.

### The IA2030 Measles & Rubella Partnership [...] Accelerated immunization activities by countries, WHO, the Measles & Rubella Partnership, and other international partners successfully prevented an estimated 59 million deaths between 2000 and 2024. Vaccination decreased an estimated measles deaths from 780 000 in 2000 to 95 000 in 2024 (1).
